open_points.subject: owner-session expiry lifecycle
open_points.text: “The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner request” conflicts with “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits” and drops their pending confirmation and uploaded file only during that pass.
open_points.question: At a time limit, does the session and its temporary state end immediately, or does it merely become invalid until the next cleanup pass formally ends it and drops that state?
options: It becomes invalid immediately but remains allocated, with its confirmation and upload, until the cleanup pass ends it.
It ends immediately at the limit and its temporary state must be dropped then; the pass only removes already-ended records.
The cleanup pass is the formal end, but all M11 facts are considered inaccessible from the limit onward.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as invalid immediately and formally remove it, including its confirmation and upload, at the next cleanup pass.

open_points.subject: owner sessions across host suspension
open_points.text: The monotonic clock “counts the time the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a suspension.”
open_points.question: Does every suspension end every owner session on resume, or does suspension merely advance the duration clocks so that only sessions whose 8-hour or 30-minute deadline passed expire?
options: Suspension only advances elapsed time; a short suspension may leave a session valid.
Any host or VM suspension ends every owner session on resume.
open_points.default_guess: Suspension advances elapsed time but does not itself end a session unless one of its deadlines was crossed.

open_points.subject: 60-second session cleanup pass
open_points.text: Registry makes a pass over the sessions “every 60 seconds from the start.”
open_points.question: When is the first pass, and what happens when a pass is delayed, lasts longer than 60 seconds, or scheduled pass times are missed during suspension?
options: Use fixed deadlines at start plus multiples of 60 seconds, coalesce missed deadlines, and never overlap passes.
Wait 60 seconds after each pass completes before starting the next.
Run immediately at process start and then every 60 seconds; run once immediately after any missed interval.
Start a pass for every fixed deadline, allowing queued or overlapping passes.
open_points.default_guess: Run the first pass 60 seconds after process start on a fixed cadence, coalesce missed deadlines into one non-overlapping pass, then resume that cadence.

open_points.subject: session admission racing the cleanup pass
open_points.text: “Validity is checked when a request arrives,” requests that pass “complete even if a limit ... comes while [they run],” while the cleanup pass decides under the session lock; session-changing requests take that lock only “after passing the session check.”
open_points.question: How is admission linearized against a cleanup pass when a request arrives before a deadline but the pass obtains the session lock and removes the session before that request obtains it, and what keeps the admitted request's session state alive until it completes?
options: The recorded arrival time wins: admission and the last-request update are made atomically, and an admitted request retains the session state until completion even if it is removed from the session table.
Lock acquisition order wins: if the pass removes the session first, the request is refused despite having arrived before the deadline.
Every request takes the session lock for its validity check and retains it for its whole execution, so cleanup waits.
open_points.default_guess: Capture arrival at ingress, atomically validate and update the last-request reading under session synchronization, and retain a reference that lets an admitted request complete after table removal.
